### A More Wakeable Window

Sleep also moves through NREM–REM cycles about every 90–110 minutes. Deep slow-wave sleep is concentrated earlier in the night, while lighter sleep and REM become more common later. Waking from deep NREM usually brings stronger sleep inertia than waking from N2, with REM in between. Near morning, reaching an easier-to-wake stage may help explain effortless awakenings—and why they vary by day.

### Practice and Morning Types

In a one-week home study of 11 people without a self-awakening habit, 82% succeeded on day seven. A separate survey found that 66 of 643 students, or 10.3%, reported the habit; they slept and woke about 30 minutes earlier and showed a morning-type tendency. This was an association, not proof of cause.

## In one line

Sometimes the impressive part is not that the body knows the time, but that it knows when waking is becoming easy.
